reason: The cited evidence shows CALPHAD is used for phase selection and can agree with experiments when databases are sufficient (E1, E2), but it does not provide specific prior evidence that CALPHAD accurately predicts fusion properties (enthalpy, entropy, volume change) for HEAs, nor that DSC calibration yields 5–10% accuracy. E3 demonstrates improved pure-element and binary descriptions but does not address multicomponent HEA fusion predictions. The key premises thus lack direct, specific support from the cited passages.
premises: CALPHAD can predict fusion-related thermodynamic properties (melting T, enthalpy, entropy) for HEAs
DSC measurements can accurately validate and calibrate CALPHAD predictions for these properties
The integrated approach achieves 5–10% accuracy for fusion properties
Configurational entropy effects in HEAs are adequately captured by CALPHAD modeling
The approach is robust when sufficient binary/ternary thermodynamic data exist
